name: read-swc-derived-partitions
description: A computed value on request: `derived: ["partitions"]` at the `swc` layer adds to each component the partitions its runnables run in — one value per declared partition whose tasks run a runnable of the component, as `{"partition": ..., "core": ...}`, in partition-name order, `core` being the partition's core where it resolves to a declared core and `null` otherwise. The value is the validator's own reading of what a partition runs, the one its partition rules read, and never a second formula; a partition name declared twice resolves to its first declaration. Set-valued (`rows: "one per value"`): a component in two partitions is two rows, and a component no partition runs has no row. It reads component types, so two instances of one type are not told apart.

context.summary: The base model with a second core, `CORE1`, carrying `PARTITION1`, and a task in `PARTITION1` running `ExampleSWC`; the base's task runs `ExampleConsumerSWC` in `PARTITION0` on `CORE0`. A third component, `UnplacedSWC`, is run by no task. So two components answer one partition each, on their cores, and the third answers no row.
context.notes: A read takes no scope and writes no audit record.

expected.notes: `UnplacedSWC` has no row: a set-valued computed value drops the row it has no value for, so "which components does no partition run" is the layer's `index` minus the components this read answers. `partitions` applies at the elements of the `swc` layer alone: asked at another layer or at a member path it is `schema-violation`, never a blank.
